rows.headline: Commodity search that lists results as you type
prototypeDoes: The latest prototype behaves the same as it did in October. The commodity script and data have not changed since then.
Testing 3 is a copy of Design Release 2.1. It uses the same commodity script, so it does not replace this behaviour.
The page holds the whole commodity list. The browser filters it on each keystroke.
Results open from the third character, with no Search press. Typing 'ca' shows nothing, and 'cat' opens the results.
Results show in a scrolling box under the field, about 5 rows high. Each commodity is a bold header row, 'Cattle (0102)', with a small checkbox for each species underneath.
Matching words are in bold. On screen the spaces around a bold word are lost, so a label reads 'Domesticcat(Feliscatus)'.
The search box is full width, with a square blue icon button joined to it. Its hidden name is 'Search'.
A hidden polite announcement says '11 results available' for 'cattle'. It counts species rows, not commodities.
For 'zzz' it shows and announces 'No results found'.
Ticking a species keeps the typed text and leaves the results open. A '1 selected' panel appears with 'Clear all'.
The panel shows each species as a chip with its Latin name and a cross to remove it, for example 'Bos taurus'.
Each tick is announced as '1 option selected', then '2 options selected'.
Escape closes the results and the selection stays. The box is emptied by Chrome's own search-box behaviour, not by the script.
Removing a chip closes the results and announces '1 option selected'. Clear all removes the panel and announces nothing.
Save and continue goes to Main import reason. When the trader comes back, the saved species is in the panel.
Germinal products uses the same search with its own hint. Typing 'semen' gives 8 commodities and 12 species rows, and announces '12 results available'.
In germinal products, 'Cattle, Semen (Bovidae)' is an ordinary checkbox, not a group row.
Without JavaScript, typing shows nothing and the icon button does nothing.
Without JavaScript, pressing Enter posts an empty choice and returns 'Select a commodity'. The trader cannot finish the page.
prototypeChanges: 9 Nov, urgent content updates: the inset now says 'health certificate' instead of ITAHC. Design Release 2.1 says 'an health certificate' and Testing 3 corrects it to 'a'. This changes the words only, not the search.
3 and 5 Nov: Testing 3 was added for user research as a copy of Design Release 2.1. It uses the same commodity script.
6 Nov, search box updates: these add a clear button to the dashboard search in Testing 3. They do not touch the commodity search.
mainDoes: Live animals searches on the server. Nothing happens until the trader presses Search or Enter.
The search box is three-quarters wide, with a separate grey 'Search' text button underneath. It does not have the joined blue icon button yet.
Results are small checkboxes grouped under the commodity code alone, '0102', with no commodity name. Matching words are in bold, with the spaces kept.
Each species label puts the Latin name first, 'Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle)'. The prototype puts the common name first.
For 'zzz' the page shows 'No results found'.
A tick appears in the '1 selected' panel only after the next press of Search, Remove or Save.
The selected panel sits under the results. It has a Remove link for each species and a grey Clear all button.
Escape clears the box through the browser, and the results stay on the page.
Nothing is announced to screen readers, because the page has no live region and no page script.
Without JavaScript the whole page works: Enter searches, and a tick plus Search updates the panel.
Save and continue goes to the Overview page.
Results come from the central commodity list through the reference data service.
On the local stack a 'cattle' search also lists germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 under live animals.
There is no germinal products set, and the type question does not offer germinal products.
Plants has no commodity search. Its genus field is a type-ahead that picks one item.
mainChanges: 23 Oct, design snagging: a shared search box with a joined blue icon button was added. Transporters and the address pickers moved onto it. The commodity page did not.
27 and 30 Oct: the search moved from a list held in the page code to the central commodity list, through the reference data service. Only rows the trader has searched for can be saved.
26 and 27 Oct: Add another commodity, Change and Save and return now go back to the right place.
6 Nov, commodities and reason: results are now ordered with bold matches, and the selected panel has Remove and Clear all. All of this works without JavaScript.
6 Nov, type question: the INS 'What are you importing?' question was added, with no germinal products option.
stillNeeds: The look can be built now, whatever design decides. Swap the commodity page onto the shared search box with the joined blue icon button, full width. It keeps the no-JavaScript search.
Search as you type needs design's answer first. Nothing should be built until then.
If design keeps it, it would add to today's server search, filtering as the trader types. It would not copy the prototype's script or put the whole list in the page.
That needs a new results feed from the frontend, a short pause between fetches, and the session's saved search rows kept in step.
It also needs Welsh for every new announcement, marked as a machine draft.
Germinal products has no page to land on. Its three criteria wait for a germinal set to exist, not only for design.
Check whether the live animals search should hide germinal codes such as semen and embryos. On the local stack they show for 'cattle'.
concerns: GOV.UK Design System has no multi-select type-ahead. Accessible autocomplete picks only one item. MoJ has no accepted multi-select search either.
The prototype is a hand-built combobox. 'Expanded' is set on a plain wrapper, and the results are a plain list of checkboxes, so screen readers do not get a recognised pattern.
The announcement area is also linked to the field's description. A screen reader may read the last announcement again whenever the field gets focus.
Once anything is ticked, a new search is announced as 'N options selected' instead of the number of results. The trader does not hear how many results there are.
Results are counted in species rows, not commodities. The spoken 'options selected' does not match the visible 'N selected'.
The prototype's results box scrolls inside itself, about 5 rows high. That is hard to use when zoomed in and on small screens.
The bold matches lose their spaces on screen in the prototype, so labels read as run-together words.
Escape emptying the field happens only in Chrome. Firefox and Safari may keep the text. The criterion should say whether the field must empty.
Without JavaScript the prototype gives the trader no way to finish the page. That breaks GOV.UK progressive enhancement. Main already works without JavaScript.
Main already has the parts for a lighter version: the shared icon search box, the bold-match helper, the live transporter filter and a status announcer. These keep the cost to maintain low.
Live animals, germinal products and plants should use one search pattern. Plants uses a single-pick type-ahead today. Germinal products does not exist on main yet.
Main's group headings show only the code, '0102'. The prototype shows 'Cattle (0102)', which is clearer for traders.
Content, not this row: main still says ITAHC in the inset. The prototype now says 'health certificate'.
refuted: The planned main caption said Save and continue goes to Commodity details. On main it goes to the Overview page.

The research said germinal products is not on main at all. That is true for the page set and the type question. But on the local stack the live animals search lists the germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 for 'cattle', so germinal products already reach the live animals page.
The research said each chip holds the species label. The chip shows the Latin name only, 'Bos taurus', grouped under 'Cattle (0102):'.
The research said the results match in bold. That is right, but on screen the spaces around a bold word are lost ('Domesticcat(Feliscatus)'). The research did not mention this.
The research did not say that removing a chip closes the results. The script closes them as well as announcing the count.
The research did not say the results box scrolls inside itself. It is a fixed-height box about 5 rows high, so most of the 11 'cattle' rows start hidden.
rows.questionForDesigner: Should the commodity search list results as the trader types? If not, we keep today's press-Search results and only add the joined blue icon button. If yes, would you accept a live filter added to the same server search (results on the page, a polite results count, and still working without JavaScript) instead of the prototype's scrolling dropdown?

rows.headline: Transit countries: add on pick and remove without a page reload
prototypeDoes: Nothing has changed for this page since October. None of the 17 newer prototype commits touch it.
Testing 2 and Testing 3 copy the Design Release 2.1 page and use the same script. Neither replaces it.
With JavaScript, the page has a custom search box. It does not use the GOV.UK accessible autocomplete.
Results show after 3 letters. A screen reader hears '1 result available'.
Picking a result adds the country straight away. There is no Add button.
The box empties and keeps focus. A screen reader hears 'Added Germany'.
The list is re-sorted A to Z on every add. Belgium added after Germany shows first.
Each Remove is a link to '#' named only 'Remove'. It does not say which country.
Remove takes the country off without a reload, and a screen reader hears 'Removed Germany'.
After a remove, focus drops to the page body.
At 12 countries the search box and its button are disabled. In the screenshot they look the same as when enabled.
The 12th add announces only 'Added Portugal'. The 'Maximum of 12' message is never heard, because it plays only when the disabled box gets focus.
The added countries are styled boxes, not a real table. A screen reader gets no table structure.
The page holds the countries as a hidden list of names, not codes.
Without JavaScript nothing can be added. Typing and pressing the search button do nothing.
Without JavaScript, Remove only adds '#' to the address.
Without JavaScript, Save and continue empties the saved list. Countries saved earlier are lost.
mainDoes: Live animals only. Plants has no transit page, and germinal products does not use this page.
A GOV.UK accessible autocomplete is built on a native select, with a secondary 'Add country' button.
The blue search square next to the box only decorates the field. Screen readers do not hear it, and clicking it moves focus to the box.
Picking a suggestion only fills the box. The country is added when 'Add country' is pressed.
Every add and remove sends the form and reloads the page, with or without JavaScript.
After the reload a screen reader hears 'Germany added.' or 'Germany removed.'.
The countries stay in the order they were added.
The added countries are a GOV.UK table. Each Remove is a button styled as a link, named 'Remove Germany', 'Remove Belgium' and so on.
At 12, the search box and Add are hidden and the page says 'Maximum of 12 countries reached. Remove a country to add another.'
The 12th add announces 'Portugal added. Maximum of 12 countries reached. Remove a country to add another.' as one message.
The server refuses an empty choice, a country not on the list, a repeat, and a 13th country.
It saves country codes.
Without JavaScript the native select ('Select a country') and Add and Remove still work. Belgium is still saved after Save and continue.
Without JavaScript nothing is announced or shown after an add or remove. The message sits in the page but only the script reads it out.
mainChanges: 23 Oct, design snagging: medium 'Enter a country' label, 'Search for a country' placeholder, 'Select a country' first option without JavaScript, no empty-state line, Remove at the right of each row. Add on pick was left out on purpose and sent to the multi-select spike.

4 Nov, arrival and transit: browser title 'Transit countries', redirect to the overview when travel is not by rail or road, territories offered as 'Territory (Country)', and Save and return to overview keeps the list.
27 Oct: the trader's own mistakes (nothing chosen, already added) are no longer logged.
No change since 1 October to how adding and removing work, or to the 'Germany added.' and 'Germany removed.' wording.
prototypeChanges: None for this page. The page and its script last changed in August.
Testing 3 is a copy for user testing. Only its form action and included partials differ.
stillNeeds: Already on main, nothing to do: Remove names its country, codes are saved, the list checks run on the server, the limit message comes in the same announcement, and the page works without JavaScript.
Gap on main whatever design decides: without JavaScript, nothing confirms an add or remove. The row asks for one. A visible message would also help sighted users with JavaScript.
Only if design keeps them: add on pick, remove without a reload, and 'Added Germany' / 'Removed Germany' instead of 'Germany added.' / 'Germany removed.'.
If remove without a reload is built, focus must go somewhere after a remove, such as the next Remove or the search box.
If design wants the prototype's A to Z order, main and the row both need changing. They keep the order added today.
The interaction designer's 9 November answers do not cover this transit question, so the row stays blocked.
concerns: GOV.UK Design System has no multi-select or 'add to list' component. The accessible autocomplete picks one value, and the MoJ library has nothing that manages a list like this.
So add on pick means our own script on top of the accessible autocomplete. Every service that reuses it would have to maintain it too.
The 9 October ruling allows only the accessible autocomplete and named MoJ components. A custom search box like the prototype's falls outside it.
Progressive enhancement: main's form posts are the right base. The prototype has no working route without JavaScript, and saving without it deletes data.
Accessibility: the prototype's results are buttons in a plain list with no arrow-key support. The accessible autocomplete already gives proper listbox behaviour and tested announcements.
Accessibility: in the prototype every Remove is just 'Remove', and focus is lost after one. Main names each Remove and avoids lost focus by reloading.
Accessibility: the prototype's added countries are styled boxes, not a table. Main uses a GOV.UK table.
Accessibility: the prototype disables the search box at 12 with no visible change and no message a screen reader hears. Main hides the controls and shows the limit in words.
GOV.UK advises against placeholder text. Both versions use 'Search for a country' as a placeholder. In the prototype it is near-black and can look like a typed answer.
Consistency: the same multi-pick question would come up for any repeating country or commodity list in live animals, germinal products and plants. One answer should cover all of them.
Wording: GOV.UK has no rule on 'Added X' or 'X added.'. Pick one and use it on every add-to-list page.
rows.questionForDesigner: Main already adds with an 'Add country' button, removes with a named Remove, announces each change with a page reload and works without JavaScript. Do you still need adding on pick and removing without a reload on top of that? If yes, should the list stay in the order added, as main does now, or be sorted A to Z like the prototype? And should the wording be 'Added Germany' or 'Germany added.'?
refuted: Research said main 'works the same with JavaScript off'. Not quite. Adding, removing and saving work, but without JavaScript nothing is announced or shown. The message is only in a data attribute that the script reads (status-announcer.js), and the capture shows nothing heard. The row's criterion for this is not met on main.
Research listed the no-JavaScript criterion as 'already on main'. True for add, remove and save. False for the 'Added' or 'Removed' confirmation that criterion also asks for.
Research called the prototype's added countries a list or table. They are styled div rows with a 'Country' header row (transit-countries.html:125-131), with no table semantics.
Planned caption said the prototype disables the search at 12. True in code (js :167-169), but the screenshot shows no visible difference from the enabled box.

Everything else checked out against the screens and code: 'Added Germany', 'Removed Germany', 'Added Portugal' alone at 12, A to Z re-sort (js :214), Remove named 'Remove' with href '#', focus on body after remove, empty hidden field without JavaScript, list cleared after a no-JavaScript save, main's 'Germany added.', 'Remove Germany' / 'Remove Belgium', and the combined 12th-country message.

rows.headline: Screen-reader wording for the country search on the origin page
prototypeDoes: The live animals and germinal products origin pages use the same hand-built country search. It is not the GOV.UK accessible autocomplete.
'Country of origin' is a heading, not a label. The box's only name is its placeholder, 'Search for a country'.
Nothing shows until you type 3 letters. After 'Fr' the list stays shut and nothing is announced.
Results are a plain list of buttons, labelled 'Country search results' for screen readers. Matches are in bold.
A hidden live region says '7 results available' after 'Fra' and '1 result available' after 'Neth'.
With no match it shows and announces 'No results found'.
Choosing a country announces 'Selected France' (or 'Selected Netherlands' on germinal products).
Arrow keys do nothing. You Tab through the result buttons, and Escape closes the list.
Without JavaScript you see the same search box, with no list to pick from. A typed country is not sent.
Save and continue then moves on to 'What are you importing?' with no error. Reopening the origin page shows an empty box.
There is no 'country required' check at all, with or without JavaScript.
None of this has changed since October. The newer Testing 3 version uses the same page and script, so it does not replace Design Release 2.1 here.
mainDoes: Live animals and plants both use the GOV.UK accessible autocomplete over a normal select.
'Country of origin' is a real label. The placeholder is 'Search for a country', with the joined blue search button.
Focusing the empty box opens the whole list and announces '40 results are available.'
Typing 'Fra' announces '7 results are available.' on live animals and '1 result is available.' on plants, because plants has a shorter country list.
Pressing Down announces 'France 1 of 7 is highlighted'.
The results list takes its name from the box's label. It has no 'Country search results' label of its own.
After you choose a country, the announcements go quiet. The screen reader reads the new value in the box instead. Nothing says 'Selected France'.
With no match it shows 'No countries found' and announces 'No search results'.
Without JavaScript the select shows, starting with 'Select a country', and saves correctly.
There is no germinal products origin page on main yet.
Welsh cannot be chosen on either frontend. Even the component's own Welsh wording is never switched on.
stillNeeds: Nothing until the designer answers. Question 13 is still open: the designer's answers of 9 November do not cover it.
If the designer keeps the component's own wording, drop this row. Nothing more is needed.

If the designer wants the results label, add 'Country search results' through the component's own option for naming its list. That means one shared change in each frontend, plus English and Welsh copy.
If the designer also wants 'Selected <country>', we would need a second live region beside the component's two. We advise against this.
In either case, the germinal products origin page has to exist first. The germinal products theme builds it.
The Welsh wording can only be checked once both frontends can switch language. No row builds that yet.
concerns: The GOV.UK Design System has no autocomplete component. The accessible autocomplete is the GOV.UK-maintained component teams use instead, and main already uses it. The MoJ component library has no country search either.
The prototype's search box has no label. A placeholder is not a label under GOV.UK guidance. This fails WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2 and 4.1.2.

The prototype's results are buttons in a list, not a listbox. Arrow keys do not work, and the expanded state sits on a wrapper rather than on the box. Screen-reader users get less than the component already gives them.
'Selected France' would repeat what the screen reader already reads from the box. A third polite live region next to the component's two risks clashing or doubled announcements.
The 'Country search results' label is low risk. The component supports it directly.
Progressive enhancement: the prototype has no working route without JavaScript, and a typed country is lost without any message. Main's select works, so main must not copy this.
The prototype never checks that a country was given. Main does, so this is not something to copy either.
Consistency: the wording must be the same on live animals, germinal products and plants. Plants also has a shorter country list, so its counts differ.
Cost to maintain: custom announcements mean overriding or adding to a third-party component, in two twin wrappers, in two languages. Every component upgrade would need them checked again.
The plants wrapper filters on a different variable from animals. The results are the same, but the two wrappers are supposed to stay identical.
rows.questionForDesigner: On the country search, can we keep the GOV.UK accessible autocomplete's own screen-reader announcements? Choose one: (a) keep them as they are, and we drop the custom wording; (b) add only the 'Country search results' list label; or (c) also announce 'Selected <country>' when a country is chosen, which repeats what the screen reader already reads and which we advise against.
refuted: The planned caption said the prototype announces '1 result available' after 'Fra'. It says '7 results available'. '1 result available' is what it says after 'Neth' on germinal products.

The research said only the no-JavaScript route lacks a 'country required' error. The prototype never checks for a country, with or without JavaScript. Its page has a slot for a country error that is never filled (routes.js 465-481, origin-of-the-import.html 50-56).
The prototype does not 'store no country'. Without JavaScript it stores an empty value (null), which wipes any earlier answer. The effect is the same: the reopened page is empty.
On main, the component's two status regions are not both used for every message. The count and the highlight can arrive in either region. That is how the component works, not a defect.
The main 'after choosing' panels say '7 options' and '1 options' are shown. The list has actually closed. The panel counted hidden options.

Everything else in the research checked out against the screens and the code: the label, the list role, the live region wording, the 3-letter minimum, the missing list label on main, the quiet announcements after a choice, Welsh never switched on, and no germinal set on main.

prototypeChanges: None for this behaviour since October. The country search script and the origin page are unchanged.
The new Testing 3 version, added 3 November, copies the same origin page and script.
The urgent content updates for user testing and the search box updates do not touch the country search.
mainChanges: Design snagging (23 October) reworked the shared autocomplete wrapper in both frontends. It added the placeholder, bold matches, the joined search button and a single change event. No announcement wording changed.
Country is now required on Save and continue, and the origin page has Save and continue on its own (3–4 November).
Back now returns to wherever the origin page was opened from (3 November). The type-ahead itself did not change.
Plants type-aheads now ignore accents, as animals already did (27 October).
Nothing since 1 October adds 'Country search results', 'Selected <country>' or Welsh switching.

rows.headline: Party pickers and the address book list filter as the trader types
prototypeDoes: Nothing about this behaviour has changed since October. The latest prototype works as it did then.
Testing 3 does not replace Design Release 2.1 here. Its picker is a copy of the 2.1 one, and every version shares the same address book page.
Party pickers (all five roles): every address for the role is on one page, with no pagination. For example, 'Showing 9 out of 9 results'.
Typing in the search box hides rows that do not match, straight away, with no page load.
It matches name, address lines and country, ignoring case. The count changes to, for example, 'Showing 1 out of 9 results'.
With no matches, it shows an empty table and 'Showing 0 out of 9 results'. There is no 'no matches' message.
Clearing the box brings every row back.
The search icon button only re-runs the filter. It never submits.
Place of origin uses the same free-text search as the other pickers. There is no country picker. Typing 'Romania' or 'Ireland' matches the country as text.
Without JavaScript, the picker search does not work. The icon button does nothing.
Pressing Enter in the search box submits 'Save and continue'. The trader lands on Consignment addresses with nothing chosen and nothing filtered.
Address book list: 'Filter addresses' is a disclosure holding a search box and a Type select. It has 4 tabs, 8 addresses a page, and pagination.
Typing redraws the table and the results line, for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2'. Every match is shown at once, from all the data loaded into the page.
The pagination is meant to hide, but it stays on screen ('1 2 3 Next'), so it offers pages that do not exist.

Changing Type filters straight away. But Type 'Consignor' leaves out addresses saved as consignor from a notification. 'Ballymore' plus 'Consignor' shows 'Showing 0 of 0', though a Ballymore consignor is listed.
With JavaScript on, Enter is swallowed. Nothing is sent and the address stays the same.
Without JavaScript, Enter submits the form and the server filters ('Showing 1-2 of 2'). The icon button still does nothing.
The address book search has a placeholder, not a hint.
mainDoes: Nothing filters as the trader types on any of this row's pages. Every search goes to the server.
Live animals pickers: 'Search' label, 'Name, address or country' hint, and a joined blue icon button that really submits.
Typing changes nothing. The search button or Enter reloads the page with the server's results, for example 'Showing 2 out of 2 results'.
This works the same with or without JavaScript.
Pickers list every address in the book, whatever its role, 5 a page with pagination. For example, 'Showing 5 out of 15 results'.
Searching a country name finds nothing. 'Denmark' gives 'No addresses match your search.', even though the hint says 'country'. Searching 'Copenhagen' finds the Danish rows.
The live animals transporter list already filters as you type. Matches are in bold, the count is announced to screen readers, and 'No transporters match your search.' shows when nothing matches.
Plants pickers (consignor, place of destination, contact) work the same way as the live animals pickers: server search, 5 a page, every role.
There are no germinal products pickers on main.

INS address book list: 'Filter addresses' is a GOV.UK details component. The search has a hint, not a placeholder. The search button is a separate green icon button on its own line, and Type is a select.
Typing or choosing a Type changes nothing until the form is submitted. Then the server filters, for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2', with a 'Clear search' link.
It shows 8 a page, with 3 sections in a sub-navigation: Origin and Consignor; Destination, Consignee and Importer; Branch. Transporters are not in it.
Without JavaScript, the list works the same way.
stillNeeds: A design answer on whether lists filter as the trader types at all. The interaction designer's 9 November answers do not cover it.
If yes, pickers first need every address for the role on one page. That is the role-filtered pickers row, still to do. Filtering a page of 5 as the trader types would mislead.
The germinal products half cannot be built until germinal products pickers exist on main.

For the address book list, live filtering means asking the server again after a short pause and swapping in the table, the results line and the pagination. The prototype loads every address into the page instead.
Drop the place of origin 'filter by typed or picked country' criterion. The prototype has no country picker. Its free-text search is already covered by the main picker criterion.

Whatever design decides, fix the country search on main. The picker hint promises country, but the address book API's text search skips the country. The INS list maps country names to codes, and the pickers should do the same.
Keep main's no-JavaScript search (a real submit button), not the prototype's.
concerns: GOV.UK Design System has no 'filter as you type' component. The nearest are the MoJ filter and the 'search as you type' pattern used on GOV.UK finders. Both keep a submit button and announce results.
Progressive enhancement: main already has a working server search. Any live filter must sit on top of it. The prototype's version breaks without JavaScript: Enter saves the page and leaves.
Screen readers: neither prototype filter announces the new count. Both results lines are plain text. Main's transporter list uses a status region, and any build should do the same (WCAG 4.1.3).
The prototype's empty state is an empty table with headers. Main says 'No addresses match your search.', which is clearer.
The prototype address book keeps its pagination on screen after filtering, and its Type 'Consignor' misses some consignors. Raise both with the designer, so testing is not based on them.
The prototype address book uses a placeholder for search guidance. GOV.UK advises a hint, and main uses a hint. Keep main's.
Consistency: on main, the transporter list filters live but the pickers and the address book list do not. Design's answer should cover all three, or say why the transporter list differs.
Consistency of the search button: pickers use a joined blue icon button. The INS address book uses a separate green icon button on its own line. Prototype uses the joined one on both.

Cost to maintain: live filtering adds client code to three frontends (animals, plants, INS) on top of the server search, and each needs tests with and without JavaScript. Reuse the transporter list's helpers (accent folding, bold matches) rather than writing a second filter.
Plants and live animals should behave the same. One shared picker change in plants covers its consignor, place of destination and contact pickers.
rows.questionForDesigner: Should these lists filter as the trader types? Main's search on the pickers and the address book list already works by pressing Search, with or without JavaScript. Options: (a) keep press-to-search everywhere, and treat the transporter list as the odd one out; (b) filter live on the party pickers only, once each shows every address for its role on one page; (c) filter live on the pickers and the address book list too, keeping the address book paged and announcing the count. And can we drop the place of origin country picker, as the prototype has?
refuted: 'Deleting letters widens the match again': not shown. With 'No' typed, only Nordic Livestock still matches, and the count stays at 'Showing 1 out of 9 results'.
'Typing in the address book filter hides the pagination': it does not. The script sets hidden, but '1 2 3 Next' stays on screen with 'Showing 1-2 of 2'. This is a prototype bug.

'Changing Type to Consignor narrows straight away': it narrows wrongly. The prototype has two internal consignor types with the same label, and the select matches only one. 'Ballymore' plus 'Consignor' gives 'Showing 0 of 0', with and without JavaScript, though a Ballymore consignor exists. Type alone gives 3 rows, and the pagination still shows.
'Searching the town matches the 2 Danish rows': it matches 3. A seeded 'Danish Meat Export ApS' in Copenhagen matches too.
'INS list: icon submit button': true, but it is a separate green button below the input, not the joined blue button the pickers and the prototype use.
The research describes the INS list as having 'tabs'. Main uses MoJ sub-navigation with 3 sections and no Transporter section. The prototype uses GOV.UK tabs with 4, including Transporter.

The research says a picker in the prototype with JavaScript off lands 'back on Roles and addresses'. The page heading is 'Consignment addresses'. The address is /roles-and-addresses, so the claim holds, but the page the trader sees is called Consignment addresses.

rows.headline: Address search that hides the address fields until a pick, in the address book, the consignee, importer and destination add pages, and the commercial transporter form
prototypeDoes: Nothing in this behaviour has changed since October. The latest prototype (7a85a03) behaves as it did at 56371e2.
Testing 3 is a copy of Design Release 2.1 for these pages. Its add-address template matches Design Release 2.1's once the folder names are ignored, so it replaces nothing.
The address book's add page (Destination, Consignee or Importer; Branch) opens on 'Search for an address' alone.
The consignee, importer and place of destination add pages inside a notification open the same way, under the Draft strip.
The address fields, contact fields and uses checkboxes are hidden by the server's markup, not by the script.
Typing 2 or more characters lists up to 8 matches from a made-up list of 500 addresses bundled into the page.
Each result shows the name in bold, then the address and country, with the typed text in bold.
Screen readers hear '1 result available' or 'No results found' through a polite live region.
Picking a result fills the fields, shows them and the uses checkboxes, hides the whole search block and announces 'Selected Acorn Farm'.
The address book's add page has no County field. The transporter form has one.
'Enter address manually' never shows on the address book or in-journey add pages. A trader whose address is not in the list has no way forward.
Saving with nothing picked lists 6 errors, from 'Enter a name or organisation name' to 'Enter a phone number', but keeps every field hidden.
Following an error link moves focus nowhere, because the field it points at is hidden.
With JavaScript off, the search input sends nothing, the search button does nothing, and the fields stay hidden after a save. That page cannot be completed.
The commercial transporter form is different. It shows the authorisation number and name, a search of Northern Ireland addresses, and a visible 'Enter address manually' link-styled button.

On the transporter form, picking a result fills the name, address lines, town and postcode, puts 'Northern Ireland' in County and reveals 'Enter contact details'. The search box stays, holding the full picked address.
On the transporter form, 'Enter address manually' shows empty fields with the country fixed to Northern Ireland.
With JavaScript off, the transporter form starts with its fields hidden and the button does nothing. A refused save shows 7 errors and finally reveals the fields.
mainDoes: No frontend on main has an address search, a hidden-fields layout or an 'Enter address manually' control.
The INS front door's add page shows every field from the start: name, address lines 1 and 2, town, County (optional), postcode, country, email and phone, then the uses checkboxes.
The INS front door's add page has no client script beyond the standard GOV.UK Frontend components. The page is the same with JavaScript off.
For Destination, Consignee or Importer the uses question is 'Address type' with Place of destination, Consignee and Importer. For Branch it has one box, 'Branch address'.
An empty save shows 7 errors, the prototype's 6 plus 'Select what this address can be used for', each beside a visible field.
Following the first error link puts focus on the Name field.
Adding a consignee from an animals notification opens the INS front door's add page with the Draft strip and 'What else should this address be used for?'.
The animals commercial transporter form shows every field from the start, with the country fixed to Northern Ireland. JavaScript makes no difference.
A completely blank transporter form is optional and saves straight to the Overview page.
Filling only the authorisation number shows 6 errors beside visible fields.
The only lookup is the address lookup spike at /address-lookup-spike. It runs in dev and local only, searches on the server and is used by no add page.
The spike searched 'SW1A 1AA' and returned 3 London addresses from the stub, each with a 'Use this address' button.
The plants frontend has no address search. Its party page is a plain typed form.
Since October, main has added the 'Choose an address type' step and the journey add page, and deleted the unused transporter search page. None of that adds search or hidden fields.
stillNeeds: Nothing can be built yet.
The designer has to decide whether the GOV.UK address pattern with every field visible will do. Their answers of 9 November do not cover this.
If the designer accepts the GOV.UK pattern, drop this row. Main already shows every field with or without JavaScript, and its error links reach visible fields.
If the designer keeps a search, it needs the real address lookup first. Today that lookup is only the dev-and-local spike.
Any search we keep is built as an enhancement on top of a page that already works without JavaScript: fields shown, and a search button that searches on the server.
Any search we keep shows the fields after a failed save, so every error link reaches a field the trader can see.
The transporter half now belongs on the INS front door's add pages, because the address book now manages transporters. Check the row's repos and its transporter dependency at the next re-distil.

Separate from this row: main uses two wordings for one error and one label. The INS front door says 'Enter a name or organisation' and 'Postcode or Zip code'. The animals transporter form says 'Enter a name or organisation name' and 'Postcode or zip code'. The prototype uses the first error wording and 'Zip' with a capital Z. Pass this to the validation-messages work.
concerns: GOV.UK pattern: the Design System's address pattern uses a postcode lookup that submits to the server with a 'Find address' button. The trader then picks from a list, and an 'Enter address manually' link is always there. The Design System has no type-ahead address search component.

Progressive enhancement: the prototype's search pages fail without JavaScript. The fields are hidden in the markup, the search input sends nothing and the button does nothing. This breaks the rule that every page must work without JavaScript.
No way forward: on the address book and in-journey add pages, 'Enter address manually' never appears, even after 'No results found'. A trader with an address that is not listed is stuck.

Accessibility: in the prototype, the error summary links point at hidden fields, so focus goes nowhere. This fails WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order) and 3.3.1 (error identification). Main does not have this problem.

Accessibility: the results are a list of buttons, not a combobox. The 'N results available' and 'Selected …' messages are custom live-region text. If type-ahead stays, use accessible-autocomplete, which is in the GOV.UK toolbox, or a server search with a button.

The 'Selected Acorn Farm' message is written into a live region inside the search block, and the prototype hides that block on a pick. Some screen readers may not read text from a region that has just been hidden.

The two places differ. The address book hides the search after a pick, so the trader cannot search again without reloading. The transporter form keeps the search and shows 'Enter address manually' from the start.
The transporter pick puts 'Northern Ireland' into County and overwrites a name the trader has already typed. A real lookup will need clear rules for which fields it fills.
On the prototype's transporter form, the error summary sits below the page heading. GOV.UK puts it at the top of the main content, above the heading. Main gets this right.
MoJ component library: it has no address-lookup component, so nothing ready-made fits there either.

Consistency: live animals and germinal products share the INS front door's add page. Plants has no search. A search built only for the front door and transporter form would split behaviour across services unless plants follows.

Cost to maintain: a custom search script with its own announcements, kept beside a no-JavaScript server search and a real lookup service, costs much more than the GOV.UK pattern or the fields-visible form main already ships.
rows.questionForDesigner: To add a UK address (destination, consignee, importer or branch) or a Northern Ireland commercial transporter, can we use the GOV.UK address pattern: a postcode 'Find address' that searches on the server, a list to pick from, and an 'Enter address manually' link that shows every field? If you want to keep the page that hides the fields until a pick, when should 'Enter address manually' show (from the start, as on the transporter form, or only after 'No results found')? And should the search box stay on the page after a pick?
refuted: Research planned a main screenshot of errors from an empty commercial transporter save. Main shows no errors there: a completely blank transporter form is optional and goes to the Overview page. Errors appear only once something is filled in, for example the authorisation number alone.
Research compared error wording but missed the count. Main's address book save shows 7 errors, not 6. It adds 'Select what this address can be used for', which the prototype never shows.

Research said main's name error reads 'Enter a name or organisation'. That holds only on the INS front door. Main's animals transporter form says 'Enter a name or organisation name', the same as the prototype, so main is inconsistent with itself.
Research said only pages that set data-hide-manual-on-select would show 'Enter address manually' after 'No results found'. No page in the prototype sets that option at all.

Research said a transporter pick reveals the address fields and contact details. It also overwrites the Name field, fills County with 'Northern Ireland', fills the search box with the full address and hides 'Enter address manually'.
Research did not mention that the prototype's address book add page has no County field, while its transporter form and every add page on main have one.
The 'Selected Acorn Farm' screenshot is an overlay showing the live region's text, not the region on the page. The region sits inside the search block, which is hidden after a pick.
Checked and true: Testing 3's add-address template matches Design Release 2.1's once the folder names are ignored.
Checked and true: the address lookup spike is routed only in dev and local.
Checked and true: the designer's answers of 9 November say nothing about addresses or the address search.

rows.headline: A Copy button beside the notification reference and the customs document code
prototypeDoes: Nothing has changed for this row since October. The latest prototype still shows the same section.
A submitted or draft notification's page has an 'Import reference numbers' section above the answers.
The section has a heading, a warning ('You must use the correct reference and code on the customs declaration or your consignment will be delayed.') and two rows.
The rows are 'Notification reference' and 'Customs document code'. The code is always C640.
Germinal products show C640 too, because the code is hard-coded.
Each row has a grey secondary button labelled just 'Copy'.
The Copy buttons do nothing. The script that copies is never loaded, in October or now.
Our test pressed both buttons and the clipboard did not change. Nothing on screen says 'Copied'.
With JavaScript off, the buttons still show and still do nothing.
Selecting the reference by hand picks up only the value, which works.
At phone width the layout breaks: the reference wraps a few characters per line, the Copy buttons sit over the values and the page scrolls sideways.
The Testing 3 version is a copy of this release and has the same section, the same two buttons and the same C640. Nothing newer replaces it.
mainDoes: Main has no 'Import reference numbers' section, no customs document code and no Copy button, in either frontend.
The live animals submitted view has the heading 'Review your notification', with 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' buttons.
The reference shows only in the strip at the top, in bold beside the 'Submitted' tag.
Selecting it by hand with a triple-click picks up the word 'Submitted' as well as the reference.
The submission confirmation panel shows 'Your reference number' with the reference. It has no customs code and no Copy button.
With JavaScript off the page looks the same, because nothing on it needs script.
Plants has the same strip and no section. We did not capture plants.
Main has no germinal products set yet, so there is nothing to capture for germinal products.
stillNeeds: First, the section itself: heading, warning and two rows of text the trader can select. That is a separate row in the overview and review work, and it has not started yet.
This row cannot be built before that, whatever design decides.
Then a design answer: do we keep the Copy buttons or drop them?
If design drops them, this row is dropped. The section's selectable text is enough.
If design keeps them, build them only when JavaScript runs, give each a clear name, and announce 'Copied' to screen readers.
Whatever design decides, the customs document code for germinal products and plants still needs confirming. The plants code row is blocked.
concerns: The GOV.UK Design System has no copy button component or pattern.
The MoJ library at the version we use (11.1.0) has no copy button either. Its earlier experimental one was rejected.
Building the buttons means writing our own JavaScript, which the house rules allow only if design makes the case for it.
In the prototype the buttons never worked, so user research has not tested whether people use them.
Progressive enhancement: the prototype shows the buttons without JavaScript. GOV.UK advises against showing a control that cannot work. Our ruling says no Copy button without JavaScript.
Accessibility: both buttons are called just 'Copy'. A screen reader user hears 'Copy, button' twice with no clue which value it copies. They need hidden text, such as 'Copy notification reference'.
Nothing tells the user that the copy worked. A 'Copied' message in a polite live region is needed so screen reader users hear it.
The section is styled by hand to look like a summary list, with a fixed-width label column. The GOV.UK summary list does the same job and works at phone width.
At phone width the fixed column causes sideways scrolling and the buttons sit over the values. That fails reflow at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10).
Live animals, germinal products and plants should behave the same. The prototype only shows the animals forms, and the hard-coded C640 is probably wrong for the other two.
Cost to maintain: custom script, its tests and the browser clipboard permission quirks, in two frontends, for a saving of one hand selection.
rows.questionForDesigner: The Copy buttons in the prototype have never worked, because their script is not loaded, so research has not tested them. Should we drop them and rely on selectable text? Or should we keep them as a JavaScript-only extra, named 'Copy notification reference' and 'Copy customs document code', with a 'Copied' message?
refuted: The research said the trader can select the reference by hand from main's journey strip. Partly wrong: a triple-click selects 'Submitted GBN-AG-26-13FGVR', so the status word comes with it, and a clean copy needs a careful drag.

The research said the fixed label column 'likely overflows' at phone width. Confirmed and worse: the reference wraps a few characters per line, the Copy buttons sit over the values and the page scrolls sideways.

The research did not mention that Testing 3 uses a different reference format. Its section shows 'GB.2026.7963918 - CHEDA', not a GBN reference, so a Copy button there would copy the ' - CHEDA' suffix too.

The research did not mention that the two pages differ around the section. The prototype's heading is the reference itself, with an 'Amend this notification' button. Main's heading is 'Review your notification', with the reference only in the strip and a 'Detailing' banner above it.

The other claims held up against the screens and the code: the copy script is not imported in application.js, the clipboard did not change after either press, the buttons show with JavaScript off, C640 is hard-coded on germinal products, and main has no clipboard code or section.
